item.title: Iran’s new ambassador to Greece meets with FM Araghchi
item.description: Mahmoud Heidari, the new ambassador of the Islamic Republic of Iran to Greece, met with Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi before departing for his diplomatic mission. During the meeting, the new ambassador outlined his proposed plan for Tehran–Athens relations and for utilizing existing capacities to expand cooperation in various fields. The foreign minister wished the new ambassador success in his mission and, referring to the historical background of relations between Iran and Greece as two ancient civilizations, stressed the need to pursue and strengthen relations between the Islamic Republic of Iran and Greece within the framework of agreements and cooperation documents between the two countries. Before being appointed as Iran’s ambassador to Greece, Mahmoud Heidari served as an assistant to the foreign minister and director general for Mediterranean and Eastern European affairs at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

item.title: Iran FM: Sustainable regional security requires collective responsibility
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi wrote in an Instagram post that the recent four-way meeting in Tehran with defense and security officials from Iran, Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan provided a valuable opportunity to advance dialogue on regional peace and security and jointly address threats and challenges, stressing that sustainable security must be ensured through regional countries’ participation without military presence or intervention by extra-regional powers.

item.title: Iranian Jordanian FMs hold phone talks discuss regional developments
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi and Jordanian Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ayman Safadi held a phone conversation on Tuesday morning to discuss regional developments. During the conversation, Araghchi outlined Iran’s positions on regional developments and stressed the need for Islamic countries and the international community to take serious action to counter the continued genocide and expansionism of the occupying Zionist regime. Recalling the devastating consequences of the US and Israeli military aggression against Iran for the region and the world, the Iranian foreign minister emphasized that restoring security to the region requires an end to the United States’ aggressive and interventionist actions, as well as containing the Zionist regime’s expansionism and warmongering. Araghchi also condemned the terrorist attack on a church in southern Jordan and expressed his condolences to the families of those killed in the incident. The foreign ministers of the two countries underscored the importance of making use of diplomacy and continuing political consultations to safeguard peace and stability in the region.

item.title: Iranian Egyptian FMs discuss regional stability by phone
item.description: Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty held a phone conversation with Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi on Tuesday morning. During the phone call, the two sides referred to the quadrilateral meeting of Iran, Pakistan, Turkey, and Saudi Arabia held in Tehran on Monday, October 26, and stressed the need to continue close consultations among regional countries to reduce tensions and establish security and stability in the region.

item.title: Araghchi urges Macron to stick to his own account of Iran’s nuclear deal
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi, reacting to French President Emmanuel Macron’s contradictory statements on Iran’s nuclear activities, wrote on X that Macron had pledged in 2018 that France would not withdraw from the JCPOA because it had signed the deal, but now claims to have always opposed any nuclear activity in Iran. “Stick to your own account, Mr. President!” Araghchi wrote.
